mission: 'An independent research fellowship that connects talented researchers with top mentors in the fields of machine alignment, transparency, and security.' Fellows do 12 weeks of research in Berkeley or London, with optional 6–12 month funded extensions, plus a longer MATS Residency. MATS says that since late 2021, 631 researchers have participated, producing more than 240 research papers, and that 10% of alumni co-founded AI safety organisations.

key_work.title: MATS Symposium talks (Summer cohorts)
key_work.plain_summary: Short presentations of scholar research, e.g. chain-of-thought interpretability and third-party frontier AI evaluations.

key_work.title: MATS alumni research
key_work.plain_summary: More than 240 papers by scholars across interpretability, evals, control and governance (MATS figure).

warnings.text: AI safety and security research is talent-constrained relative to the pace of AI progress (implied by MATS's mission; Ryan Kidd talks).

recommendations.text: Pair promising researchers with experienced mentors for intensive, full-time research.
Encourage alumni to found new AI safety organisations ('AI safety needs founders' — Ryan Kidd).
